      "value": 59,

      "compared": "animal research articles vs. reporting requirements",
      "species": [],
      "n": 271,
      "n_counts": "articles",
      "verbatim": "The survey, commissioned by the National Centre for the Replacement, Refinement and Reduction of Animals in Research (NC3Rs), a UK Government-sponsored scientific organisation, found that only 59% of the 271 randomly chosen articles assessed stated the hypothesis or objective of the study and the number and characteristics of the animals used (i.e., species/strain, sex and age/weight)."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "percentage of papers not reporting randomisation",
      "value": 87,

      "measures": "share of papers that did not report using randomisation to reduce bias in animal selection and outcome assessment",
      "compared": "animal research articles vs. reporting requirements",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "papers",
      "verbatim": "Most of the papers surveyed did not report using randomisation (87%) or blinding (86%) to reduce bias in animal selection and outcome assessment."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "percentage of papers not reporting blinding",
      "value": 86,
      "unit": "percent",

      "compared": "animal research articles vs. reporting requirements",

      "statistic": "percentage of publications fully describing statistical methods and presenting results with a measure of precision or variability",
      "value": 70,

      "verbatim": "Only 70% of the publications that used statistical methods fully described them and presented the results with a measure of precision or variability."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "percentage of journal articles not reporting the number of animals used",
      "value": 4,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "share of journal articles that did not report the number of animals used anywhere in the methods or the results sections",
      "compared": "animal research articles vs. reporting requirements",
      "species": [],
      "n": 271,
      "n_counts": "journal articles",
      "verbatim": "Our review found that 4% of the 271 journal articles assessed did not report the number of animals used anywhere in the methods or the results sections."
    }
  ],
  "headline_index": 0,
  "what_the_study_did": "The study reviewed the reporting quality of bioscience research, particularly animal research, and developed the ARRIVE guidelines to improve it.",
  "what_it_found": "A significant proportion of published animal research articles lack essential details regarding study design, methods, and results, hindering their utility and reproducibility.",
  "key_quotes": [
    {
      "quote": "The survey, commissioned by the National Centre for the Replacement, Refinement and Reduction of Animals in Research (NC3Rs), a UK Government-sponsored scientific organisation, found that only 59% of the 271 randomly chosen articles assessed stated the hypothesis or objective of the study and the number and characteristics of the animals used (i.e., species/strain, sex and age/weight).",
      "topic": "Reporting omissions"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Most of the papers surveyed did not report using randomisation (87%) or blinding (86%) to reduce bias in animal selection and outcome assessment.",
      "topic": "Bias reduction reporting"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Only 70% of the publications that used statistical methods fully described them and presented the results with a measure of precision or variability.",
      "topic": "Statistical reporting"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Our review found that 4% of the 271 journal articles assessed did not report the number of animals used anywhere in the methods or the results sections.",
      "topic": "Animal numbers reporting"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Convincing evidence is emerging that CONSORT improves the quality and transparency of reports of clinical trials.",
      "topic": "Guideline impact"
    },
    {
      "quote": "The ARRIVE guidelines consist of a checklist of 20 items describing the minimum information that all scientific publications reporting research using animals should include, such as the number and specific characteristics of animals used (including species, strain, sex and genetic background); details of housing and husbandry; and the experimental, statistical and analytical methods (including details of methods used to reduce bias such as randomisation and blinding).",
      "topic": "ARRIVE guidelines"
    }
  ]
